scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ochre. I read the Jeveration paper, its code and its checkpoint, and ran it.

steps.say: A frozen Qwen vision language model reads the prompt, then one decision token per image code.

steps.caption: 128 codes from an 8,192-entry codebook
steps.say: A head picks every code at once, and a decoder paints them.

scenes.title: Why parallel choices need a shared state

legend: Each cell on its own: a double exposure
One state for every cell: one picture
A new state: a different whole picture

steps.say: Sample every code on its own and each follows its own picture. The paper proves the miss equals the total correlation.
steps.term: Total correlation: how much the codes depend on each other

steps.say: So every position reads one shared random state, and they agree on one picture.
A new state gives a different picture, still in one piece.

scenes.title: Teaching it to use the state

steps.say: Trained on images directly, the model ignores the state. So a masked model learns the image distribution first.
Sampled in one pass, it scores point three two on GenEval.

steps.term: Distribution matching: the teacher judges the student's own samples
steps.say: Then the one-pass student is trained against that teacher, until its codes fit together.
The released checkpoint reaches point seven four.

scenes.title: How much faster, and against whom
scenes.say: The headline speedup is against a slow autoregressive model. Against the fastest unified model in the same table, it is about one point two times.

scenes.title: On an RTX 3090, ms per image
scenes.say: On a three ninety it takes about a hundred and forty-five milliseconds, two thirds of it the backbone. And each position's choice is far from confident.

steps.caption: Show-o Turbo-512, 94.1 ms: not plotted
steps.say: The paper's own plots leave out Show-o Turbo, the closest unified model.
On preference scores it sits below most one-step diffusion models.

steps.caption: 67.7 mIoU on NYUv2
steps.say: The same weights also segment rooms and estimate depth and normals.
